content:
Asian International Catering Group withdraws applications for multiple stores

Less than a few days after the new measures took effect, chain restaurants have already 'backed out'. Among them, the '100% Restaurant' brand, which had 12 branches approved, only mentioned 8 branches on social media that allow dogs to enter. The Ma On Shan Kam Ying Court branch posted a handwritten notice last Friday (10th) saying 'This store has cancelled its dog-friendly restaurant status', later replaced with a sign reading 'Please do not bring pets inside'. The same group's 'Milk Café' also had 13 branches approved, but social media only mentioned 12. The 'Eat Dot Eat Restaurant' originally on the list at Tsui Ping (North) Shopping Centre in Kwun Tong has also disappeared from the list updated by the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department on July 11th.

The Asian International Catering Group, which operates the above restaurants, stated on social media last Saturday (11th) that after evaluation, some branches, due to factors such as store space, seating layout, entrance and exit traffic flow, and customer flow, may affect other customers' dining experience, on-site order, and safety if dogs are allowed to enter. Prioritising ensuring all customers enjoy a comfortable and safe dining environment, the group decided to proactively apply for cancellation of the relevant permits for individual branches; if individual branches have suitable conditions, reapplication is not ruled out.

When responding to media inquiries, the group confirmed that the '100% Restaurant' branches at Tseung Kwan O Ming Tak Shopping Centre, Fanling Eight Argent Place, and V WALK in Nam Cheong are processing cancellation procedures. Staff at the Milk Café Tuen Mun Times Square branch also told reporters that due to facility issues they cannot accommodate dogs and have surrendered their licences.

In addition, McDonald's, which originally had four approved branches, previously told the media that the official implementation date and details would be announced later. Checking the latest list, the Yau Tong Yau Lai Shopping Centre branch has disappeared. The 'One Pot Noodle' at Mei Foo Mall in Lai Chi Kok, Le Méridien Cyberport South Block, Chông Èr in Mong Kok, and the shuttered Alva House by Yat Hotel Sha Tin, have also vanished from the list, bringing the cumulative total to 9 restaurants removed from the list. Additionally, Café de Coral, which had two approved branches, has a notice stating the pet-friendly arrangement is postponed until this afternoon (13th) at 3pm. Reporters who went to observe found that the Café de Coral at Tai Wai Wai Fong will delay for seven days until the 20th of this month, while the Café de Coral at Tsuen Wan Lok Yau House will implement as scheduled today. Reporters waited from 5:30pm to 7:30pm but did not see any dog owners bringing their pets.

M+, Tseung Kwan O Plaza restaurants withdraw due to venue issues

Some restaurants had to cancel due to deed of mutual covenant and venue clause issues. Nodi, a café located in the basement of M+, has applied to the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department for withdrawal because M+ museum venue rules explicitly prohibit dogs other than service dogs from entering. In addition, three restaurants originally on the list at Tseung Kwan O Plaza—Café de Coral, Shanghai Pan-fried Bun King, and Oliver's Super Sandwiches—were removed on the eve of policy implementation. The property management company told the media that the building's deed of mutual covenant does not permit dogs to enter the shopping mall premises, so diners cannot bring dogs into restaurants within the mall. However, the media discovered a pet grooming shop inside the mall.

Restaurants warned over open-flame cooking on dining tables

In addition, some approved restaurants have been reported for violations. Media reports indicate that at least two restaurants allowing dogs have used open-flame appliances to cook or heat food on dining tables. The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department conducted inspections and issued immediate stern warnings, ordering them not to repeat the offence. It reiterated that the licensing condition states 'food must not be cooked or heated on dining tables at any time', emphasising that any further violations of conditions and legal requirements will result in immediate enforcement action; similar behaviour at other restaurants will also face direct enforcement without any grace period.

Some restaurants set time slots and quantity limits, no dogs on weekends

FEHD guidelines state that restaurants may, as needed, set their own time periods and zones for allowing dogs to enter. Some pet-friendly restaurants have restrictions: one '100% Restaurant' branch's notice states that dogs cannot be accommodated Monday to Sunday from 11:30am to 4:30pm and from 6pm to 8pm, with a maximum of 3 dogs allowed. If neighbouring diners feel disturbed, dogs must be placed back on the floor; excessive barking must be calmed or the dog taken away. If staff need to clean up excrement, an additional HK$100 cleaning fee applies. A 'Milk Café' branch posted a similar notice, stating that dogs are not accepted Monday to Friday from 11:30am to 6:30pm, and all day on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays. Another restaurant stated that bringing dogs requires WhatsApp reservation.

The new measures have sparked controversy. Multiple photos circulating online show dog owners letting their dogs lick utensils directly and allowing them to place front paws on dining tables. Many restaurants' posts about allowing dogs have drawn numerous comments saying 'won't patronise'. One Kowloon City district restaurant said it received nearly 30 complaints on the first day of implementation. FEHD Director Yuen Yuk-kin said today that 20 complaints have been received so far, involving issues such as dog leash length and seating position of dogs. The department has conducted approximately 2,300 inspections and issued a certain number of verbal warnings.
